rationale: Hapax in the kephalaion vocabulary. Position in refining-sequence (purify → X → adorn → paint as icon) and likely connection to Greek ἀκμή/ἀκμάζω 'peak, ripen' supports a perfecting/tempering sense. Could be a Greek-derived metallurgical or agricultural verb adapted into Coptic with Lyc. ⲝ-onset.

Greek μεταγγισμός 'pouring from one vessel into another, transfusion' — the technical Manichaean term for the transmigration of the soul of the unperfected catechumen into a new body. Distinct from μετενσωμάτωσις/μετεμψύχωσις. Should be retained as a Greek-derived technical term ('metangismos') or rendered 'transmigration.'

Greek εἰκών. In this kephalaion clearly refers to Mani's painted Picture-Book (the Eikōn / Middle-Persian Ārdhang) as a written/depicted artifact paralleling his other writings ('every matter you have written to the Icon'). Should be capitalized as the title of a specific Manichaean canonical work.

Lyc. ⲡⲉϩ-ⲉ-ⲍⲟ 'his face' with epenthetic ⲉ between possessive prefix and ⲍⲟ = ϩⲟ 'face' (cf. ⲡⲍⲟ in glossary). Used here in Manichaean recasting of Matt 6:21 substituting 'face' (= the painted icon-face of the soul) for 'treasure.'

Lyc. ϣⲓⲛⲉ ⲁⲣⲁ⸗ 'inquire of, request from.' Here in habitual ϣⲁⲩ-ϣⲛⲧⲩ̄ ⲁⲣⲁϩ 'they habitually request from him.' The -ⲩ̄ ending may be an inflectional contraction of the verb stem before the prepositional phrase.
